title: Active learning optimizes cell-free systems to enable genome-wide transcriptomic profiling
summary: Bayesian optimization with automated high-throughput experimentation explored over 1.6 million buffer compositions and experimentally tested 653. An mRNA-optimized buffer gave a 20-fold higher mRNA yield and a trade-off buffer 13-fold while keeping protein production. Direct RNA-seq of the T7 phage transcriptome in these systems revealed distinct regulatory layers compared with purified T7 polymerase and infected bacteria.
ai_technology: Active-learning workflow with Bayesian optimization over buffer compositions

evidence.tested: 653 buffer compositions tested experimentally; direct RNA-seq of the T7 transcriptome.
evidence.unknown: One phage transcriptome studied; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian optimization selected which buffers to test, finding the high-yield formulations.
